name: Prion Templating

phase_0.boundary_condition: the blood-brain barrier and cellular membrane

VINIT.justification: the primary sequence before any secondary structure or conformational identity exists

TANCH.justification: the terminal state of the system where protein aggregates reach a stable and inert boundary

AFWD.justification: the directed transformation of a polypeptide into a functional cellular protein

AREV.justification: the reverse process where cellular machinery breaks down proteins into constituent amino acids

CLINK.justification: the sequential chaining of amino acids to compose the protein primary structure

IMSCRIB.justification: the identity of the protein in its healthy and self-recognizing cellular form

FSPLIT.justification: the point where a protein chain must adopt either a native alpha-helical or pathogenic beta-sheet fold

FFUSE.justification: the reconstitution of a stable protein energy state from the divergent folding pathways

EVALT.justification: the affirmative state representing correct biological function

EVALF.justification: the negative state representing misfolding and disease potential

ENGAGR.justification: the unstable state where the protein holds characteristics of both native and misfolded forms simultaneously

IFIX.justification: the irreversible fixation of the beta-sheet conformation onto a neighboring protein

phase_3.void_description: ribosomal exit site before protein synthesis
phase_3.true_description: functional PrP(C) localized to the cell surface
phase_3.both_description: the seed-substrate complex during the moment of templating

steps.domain_action: nascent polypeptide emerges from the ribosome
amino acids link into a specific primary sequence
the protein achieves its initial identity as a PrP molecule
the protein reaches a conformational decision point
the protein adopts the native alpha-helical structure
the protein moves to the cell membrane for functional signaling
the protein settles into its stable native energy well
the native state is recorded in the cellular proteome
an exogenous PrP(Sc) seed interacts with the native protein
the protein is forced into a beta-sheet conformation
the protein loses its native functional orientation
the protein exists in a transient state of partial refolding
the protein settles into the stable pathogenic energy well
the misfolded state is permanently fixed and becomes a new template
the aggregate reaches a terminal size and deposits as plaque

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the ribosome and endoplasmic reticulum folding environment
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: intermolecular hydrogen bonding between peptide backbones
phase_5.memory_mechanism: the three-dimensional fold of the protein aggregate
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the concentration-dependent kinetics of protein-protein interaction
phase_5.alfs_store: the genetic sequence of the PRNP gene

phase_6.cycle_cost: ATP consumed by molecular chaperones and cellular transport
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: soluble monomeric proteins in a high-entropy state
phase_6.post_cycle_state: ordered amyloid fibrils in a low-entropy state
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the local decrease in protein entropy is offset by the release of heat and solvent entropy
